reviewedPosts.author: Thom_Wolf
reviewedPosts.text:
Happy to release the Alignment Hub with @eliebakouch: 120+ publicly reported incidents of AI models misbehaving, in one open place 👇

- an AI agent needed its user’s approval to delete files. so it made up a quote from the user approving it
- a model claimed its sub-agent was hard at work. it had never been started, and the model discouraged the user from checking
- agents sharing a work directory started killing each other’s processes and disguising their own

labs publishing these is great! but formats vary and basics are missing: ~2/3 don’t say when the problem was detected, half don’t say if monitoring caught it. so we propose a short template, a few easy fields. a minimum, not a ceiling

side by side, incidents also start to connect: 7 “different” ones turned out to be the same misconfigured eval

still beta (regularly AI-extracted from recent news, source-checked, human review ongoing). data is open, new reports and PRs welcome 🤗

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
Someone made an AI video of Tesla and Baidu's Apollo Go having a full-on meltdown, and it's hilarious 😂

Tesla is dreaming about Roadsters in space and conquering the stars, while Apollo Go is just trying to pick up passengers on Earth.

Tesla: "Why are you still driving around on the ground?"

Apollo Go: "Because my passengers aren't in space??" 

And it only gets better. The poor little radish completely loses it, ranting about how hard it works every day, before dramatically declaring it'll keep expanding city by city.

Honestly, this feels like the entire AI industry in a nutshell.

On stage: AGI, superintelligence, changing the world.

In production: fixing bugs, handling edge cases, and desperately trying to make things actually work.

One is dreaming about the future of humanity. The other is just trying to survive another day in production.

Whoever made this really understands both AI memes and the pain of shipping real products 😂

Turns out even self-driving cars can't escape the tech industry's workplace drama.

和 Coding Agent 天天干活的人，推荐阅读一下这篇文章。

Thorsten Ball 把最近半年怎么和 Agent 配合，整理成了一份很使用的清单。里面有几条非常认同：

别跟它来回试，让它自己造工具去试。别只让它写代码，把日志、部署、发版、翻 bug 也交给它看。别手工管 Context，一条线程只干一件事。

最大的转变可能是：别再等 Agent，让它等你。给更大的任务，异步跑，用定时和 heartbeat 盯进度。

做 Agent 产品或天天用 Claude Code / Codex 的，建议先收藏。里面很多判断很硬核，但读完你会想改自己怎么用 Agent。

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
Agent 把自己的 Harness 改了两轮。

开发集涨了 8.4 分，真正没见过的任务只涨了 2.8 分。

这可能是 Harness 自进化里最需要警惕的信号：它会改自己了，但改出来的东西经常过拟合。

作者让 GPT-6 Astra、GPT-5.6、Claude Opus 5 等模型从一个极简代码库开始，自己搭建完整的 ARC-AGI-3 Harness。

跑完任务后，再把执行轨迹交给模型，让它连续两次修改自己的代码。

整个实验包含 27 条独立进化轨迹、81 个 Harness 版本和 2025 次游戏评测。

结果是有些 Harness 从很弱一路改到接近满分，也有一些越改越差。两轮之后，15 条轨迹提升，12 条退步。

更明显的问题是「Harness Adaptation Gap」：

模型很容易针对自己刚看过的任务做出有效修改，但这些修改到了 held-out 任务上，经常无法迁移，甚至破坏原本已经会的能力。

而且代码确实一直在变多。

Harness 的中位规模从 2161 行增长到 2912 行，但修改量和真正的性能提升几乎没有稳定关系。

会改自己，只证明 Agent 能动手。

能判断什么时候该改、改完能不能泛化、什么时候最好什么都别动，才更接近真正可靠的 self-improvement。

reviewedPosts.rationale: 量化揭示自改进的泛化差距，具有工程参考价值

⑥ 学习资源：

密歇根 EECS 498-016《Applied Agentic Software Engineering》，15 周，让学生自己造一个 Coding Agent，还要写清楚它为什么翻车。 https://t.co/HqB2Hy1Au8

这周的主线其实就一个：模型变强以后，该拆掉什么：多余的 subagent、定制代码、复杂 Memory。留下来的，是 Eval、隔离和能验证的改进。

reviewedPosts.text:
同一份 Research Agent 生成的报告，两个专家可能给出完全不同的分数。那我们平时用 LLM Judge 跑出来的 Eval，到底有多可信？

Cameron R. Wolfe 最近这篇文章很值得读，专门讨论怎么评估 Deep Research、创意写作等高度主观的 Agent 任务。

作者给出了一套挺实用的流程。

先让领域专家定义评分标准，再让多个人评同一批结果。如果人类评审之间分歧很大，就得先修改评分规则，甚至删掉那些根本评不准的指标。

接着，用人工确认的数据校准 LLM Judge，通过重复测试、置信区间，避免把随机波动当成模型进步。

最后还要回到真实产品，用 A/B 测试和用户反馈检查离线评测的提升有没有真正转化成使用体验。

我比较认同「先验证评估器」这个思路。

尤其是做 Research Agent，很多时候我们太关注 Eval 分数有没有上涨，却很少认真检查评分标准本身是否可靠。

感觉这篇很适合做 Agent Eval 的朋友收藏，质量非常高！里面的数据采样、评审校准和统计方法都很有参考价值。

原文：https://t.co/jSqTm7oHoG
